raw_response:
I've been farming these 7.5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. I'm 64, and it's just me and my wife at home these days — our children are working in the city. At my age, I have to think hard about what my back can handle and how far our cash will stretch.

Cotton has always been our backbone. I know cotton. I know when the bollworms come, I know which fields hold water and which don't. But cotton picking is brutal on an old man's back. That's why I started growing stevia on 1.5 mu a few years ago — the purchase station opened in town, and stevia you just cut and dry, no hunched-over picking for weeks. So this year, 6 mu for cotton, 1.5 mu for stevia.

For cotton, I'll plant in mid-to-late April with improved seeds from the supply store. I stopped saving my own seeds years ago — the yield drops too much. I'll put down compound fertilizer as base before planting, around 25 kg per mu, then topdress with urea when the plants start flowering. The extension agent says I could push to 18 kg nitrogen per mu, but I've found 14 kg is plenty on my soil, and every jin of fertilizer I save is cash in my pocket. I'll irrigate twice — once when the buds are setting and again at peak flowering. The well water is metered now, so I watch it like a hawk. For pests, I'll spray for bollworms three or four times. I used to carry the backpack sprayer myself, but last year my shoulder acted up, so I'll hire the drone service for at least one pass.

The stevia is simpler. I buy seedlings and plant them in late April or early May. It doesn't need much — some base fertilizer, maybe 8 kg nitrogen per mu total, and one or two irrigations in the summer. I cut it two or three times from July through September and dry the leaves. The yield isn't huge, but the price is steady and the labor is manageable for us.

Labor is what keeps me up at night. My wife and I can handle the day-to-day weeding and tending, but when cotton picking season comes in September and October, we'll need hired hands. I reckon we'll need about 18 days of hired labor for the cotton — mostly pickers — and maybe a couple days for the stevia harvest. At 100-120 yuan per day, that adds up fast, but there's no choice. Two people can't pick 6 mu of cotton alone.

I'm budgeting about 4,850 yuan total for inputs and hired help this season. It's a stretch, but cotton prices have been decent and I need to keep some cash reserve for my wife's medicine. If the weather cooperates, I'm hoping for about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton and maybe 120 kg per mu of dried stevia leaves. Nothing fancy — just steady, like it's always been.
